newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan police injure protesters in court.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan police injure protesters in court.

text.p: A dozen Moroccans including a woman and child were seriously injured on Friday when police dispersed supporters of a leftist group during their trial, lawyers said.
The Beni-Mellal court, in central Morocco, was trying 18 members of the opposition Avant-Garde Democratique Socialiste Party (PADS), who campaigned for the boycott of communal elections on June 13.

"The violent intervention of security forces inside Beni Mellal court led to serious injuries of at least 12 people, including a woman and child," a lawyer member of the independent Moroccan Human Rights Association (AMDH) told Reuters.
Police moved in to disperse 400 supporters of the defendants, who chanted slogans and demanded the release of the arrested PADS members, the lawyer said.
"This is a violation of basic human rights and speech freedom which are in principle guaranteed by Morocco's constitution," said Ahmed Benjelloun, a prominent lawyer and leader of PADS.
More than 30 lawyers were present in the court when police broke in and "savagely beat up PADS supporters," he said.
Among Morocco's dozen active parties, the PADS was the only opposition group to call for the boycott of local elections.
A total of 130 PADS militants were arrested of which 92 were tried in different provinces of the country and faced up to two months in jail, the AMDH said.
Justice and Human Rights Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
